description: molcajete remote desktop performance: server frame pipeline, browser and network, gateway, CPU profiles, session logs

panels.title: Open tunnels
panels.description: WebSocket tunnels currently open on the gateway

panels.title: Active sessions
panels.description: Sessions molcajeted holds to remote desktops

panels.title: Frames sent
panels.description: Frames (sync) molcajeted sends per second

panels.title: Frame build p95
panels.description: Server CPU time to diff and encode one frame. Above 33 ms, 30 fps is out of reach

panels.title: ack p95
panels.description: From sending a frame until the browser has drawn and acknowledged it (includes the network round trip). molcajeted measures it per protocol, for every client together; per session it is in the Sessions table

panels.title: Browser lag p95
panels.description: From the browser receiving a frame to drawing it (decoding + GPU), for the clients selected by Browser and Device

panels.title: Frame build time
panels.description: Distribution of one Display::flush. When this is high, server CPU is the bottleneck

panels.title: CPU per flush phase (share of one core)
panels.description: CPU used by each phase of flush; 100% is one full core. Optimize the thickest layer first. pixels includes image encoding

panels.title: Image encode time p95
panels.description: Time to encode one image as PNG/JPEG

panels.title: Encoding throughput
panels.description: Pixels encoded per second (Mpx/s)

panels.title: Compression (bytes/pixel)
panels.description: Encoded bytes ÷ pixels. Lower means less bandwidth

panels.title: Video encode time p95
panels.description: Encoding one video frame (including the ffmpeg round trip). Above 33 ms, video mode cannot keep up

panels.title: Encoded bytes per frame p95
panels.description: Image bytes in one frame (before base64)

panels.title: Socket write wait p99
panels.description: Time molcajeted is blocked writing to the gateway. High values mean the gateway or browser cannot keep up (backpressure)

panels.title: Received from the remote server
panels.description: Bytes molcajeted reads from the remote server (RDP, VNC, SSH)

panels.title: Remote update decode time
panels.description: Decoding one update from the remote server (p50 and p95)

panels.title: Images per frame
panels.description: Images (PNG, JPEG, zstd) sent in one frame: each costs the client a decode

panels.title: Copies found by detection
panels.description: Copies per second that scroll and move detection found (the result of the scroll and moves phases above)

panels.title: Remote decode CPU (share of one core)
panels.description: Time spent decoding updates from the remote server, per second of wall time

panels.title: Frames per second: remote server and sent
panels.description: Frames the RDP server ended on the graphics pipeline, and frames sent to the client. Sent well below the server's during video: frames are being merged

panels.title: Time between frames
panels.description: Time between a frame and the one before it, within a run of frames (p50 and p95). Even playback keeps the two close together

panels.title: Frames more than 40 ms apart
panels.description: Share of frames that came more than 40 ms after the one before, within a run of frames. During a 30 fps video this is the share of frames that were merged or held back (stutter)

panels.title: Server ack vs RTT, frame arrival and browser lag (p95)
panels.description: ack is roughly tunnel RTT + frame arrival + browser frame lag. The tunnel ping is one small message, so it does not show how long a large frame takes to cross the link: that is frame arrival (first drawing instruction to sync, measured in the browser). The browser series follow the Browser and Device selection; the ack is for every client together

panels.title: Browser fps
panels.description: Frames per second the browser actually applied (p50, p10)

panels.title: Backlog
panels.description: Operations not yet drawn in the browser (p95) and frames not yet acknowledged at the server (p95)

panels.title: Browser lag p95 by client
panels.description: From the browser receiving a frame's sync to applying it, per kind of client (browser engine and device)

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_frame_lag_seconds_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Frame arrival p95 by client
panels.description: From a frame's first drawing instruction to its sync, per kind of client: how long its data took to arrive

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_frame_receive_seconds_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Client apply time (reported to molcajeted)
panels.description: How long molcajete clients say a frame took to apply (decoding and drawing, without waiting behind earlier frames). It sets their frame interval

panels.title: Clients over the time range
panels.description: p95 over the selected time range per kind of client. Two clients of the same kind share a row: see the Sessions table for each session

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_frame_lag_seconds_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_frame_receive_seconds_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_rtt_seconds_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, browser, device) (rate(molcajete_client_frames_fps_bucket{browser=~"$browser", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Relayed traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second relayed by the gateway

panels.title: Handshake time p95
panels.description: molcajeted handshake and remote connection when opening a tunnel

panels.title: Closed tunnels (by status)
panels.description: Tunnels closed per Guacamole status code; 0 is a normal close

panels.title: molcajeted CPU flamegraph
panels.description: CPU samples in the selected time range; wider bars use more CPU. Narrow the range to a slow period. Idle periods are empty

panels.title: gateway CPU flamegraph
panels.description: CPU samples in the selected time range; wider bars use more CPU. Narrow the range to a slow period. Idle periods are empty

panels.title: Session summaries (display summary)
panels.description: Summary logged when a molcajeted session ends. Look for sessions with high flush_ms_max or client_ack_ms_max

targets.expr: {namespace="molcajete", container="molcajeted"} |= "display summary" | json | line_format `{{.span_id}} {{.protocol}} {{printf "%.0f" (float64 .duration_s)}}s frames={{.frames}} fps={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .fps_avg)}} | flush avg/max={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .flush_ms_avg)}}/{{printf "%.1f" (float64 .flush_ms_max)}}ms | ack avg/max={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .client_ack_ms_avg)}}/{{printf "%.1f" (float64 .client_ack_ms_max)}}ms | png={{.png_images}} ({{printf "%.2f" (float64 .png_ms_avg)}}ms) jpeg={{.jpeg_images}} ({{printf "%.2f" (float64 .jpeg_ms_avg)}}ms) video={{.video_frames}} ({{printf "%.1f" (float64 .video_encode_ms_avg)}}ms)`

panels.title: Browser reports (client report)
panels.description: Performance summary the browser sends every 10 seconds. guacd_id is molcajeted's connection id (span_id of its display summary)

targets.expr: {namespace="molcajete", container="gateway"} |= "client report" | json | line_format `{{.connection}} {{.mode}} {{.browser}}/{{.device}} {{.guacd_id}} | fps avg/min={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .fps_avg)}}/{{printf "%.1f" (float64 .fps_min)}} | lag avg/max={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .frame_lag_ms_avg)}}/{{printf "%.1f" (float64 .frame_lag_ms_max)}}ms | arrival max={{printf "%.1f" (float64 .frame_receive_ms_max)}}ms | rtt={{.rtt_ms_avg}}ms | queued max={{.queued_ops_max}} | {{.display_width}}x{{.display_height}}`

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: WARN/ERROR logs from the gateway and molcajeted

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: One row per tunnel over the time range, from the logs. Browser columns come from the client reports (p95 of the 10-second averages, and the largest maximum); the ack columns from molcajeted's display summary, logged when a session ends, joined on its connection id (guacd_id).

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {namespace="molcajete", container="gateway"} |= "client report" | json | unwrap frame_lag_ms_avg | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id, tunnel_id, connection, browser, device)
max_over_time({namespace="molcajete", container="gateway"} |= "client report" | json | unwrap frame_lag_ms_max | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id)
max_over_time({namespace="molcajete", container="gateway"} |= "client report" | json | unwrap frame_receive_ms_max | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id)
avg_over_time({namespace="molcajete", container="gateway"} |= "client report" | json | unwrap rtt_ms_avg | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id)
max_over_time({namespace="molcajete", container="molcajeted"} |= "display summary" | json | label_format guacd_id=span_id | unwrap client_ack_ms_avg | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id)
max_over_time({namespace="molcajete", container="molcajeted"} |= "display summary" | json | label_format guacd_id=span_id | unwrap client_ack_ms_max | __error__="" [$__range]) by (guacd_id)
